speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an adolescent experiencing delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility. To begin our evaluation, have you noticed any specific fractures from minor falls or injuries in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency) causing ambiguous genitalia at birth, precocious/pubertal adrenal androgen excess leading to delayed true menarche, severe acne, and potential bone fragility due to chronic glucocorticoid deficiency or altered bone mineralization.
